subject: Satellite proxy + egress IP authorization for private endpoints
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@starlighthealth.io>; netops@starlighthealth.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Satellite proxy + egress IP authorization for private endpoints

Hi Alice / Starlight netops team,

Following our onboarding call last week, we are preparing to route Redwood Private data-plane egress (model payloads and KV cache fetches) through the partner-managed satellite proxies you maintain in Starlight's DMZ. To proceed we need a formalized allowlist and a small set of operational controls from your side so our security/compliance teams can sign off.

High-level asks from Redwood: 
- A stable set of public IPv4 addresses (or short, well-documented pools) for the satellite proxies (used by data-plane egress) and for the control-plane callbacks.
- Clarification on where TLS terminates (edge vs origin) and whether mutual TLS will be used for control-plane calls.
- Acceptable DNS names + cert fingerprints if TLS is terminated in the DMZ and re-originated internally.
- Expected IP rotation cadence (if any) and a webhook or ticket hook to notify us before any planned change.
- Any mandatory HTTP proxy headers or mTLS CA bundles we must include.

Attachments: controlplane-egress-uri-list.csv (initial URIs we will call), satellite-proxy-deployment-diagram.png. I will follow up with an egress IP rotation schedule once we have the ranges.

We're aiming to complete the allowlist approvals and a short ops dry-run by next Thursday (2027-04-07). Can you confirm who on your side will sign the IP ranges and whether Starlight can guarantee a 72-hour change notice?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@starlighthealth.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, netops@starlighthealth.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite proxy + egress IP authorization for private endpoints

Karthik — thanks for the clear list. Opening with answers to your bullets: 

- Stable IPs: we can provide a /29 (6 usable) for the satellite proxy frontends plus two static NAT IPs for control-plane callbacks; final ranges attached after internal ticketing. We will limit changes to maintenance windows.
- TLS termination: currently, our DMZ terminates TLS at the proxy (TLS edge) and then re-establishes TLS inbound to your origin. For the control-plane map we can support mTLS (client certs) if Redwood supplies a CA bundle.
- Cert fingerprints: will provide cert chain fingerprints via secure vault link (we prefer vault-based exchange over in-email attachments).
- IP rotation: normal cadence is quarterly unless an incident requires immediate rotation. We can commit to 72-hour notice for planned changes if this is elevated via our PAM workflow.

Two clarifying questions: 
1) Do you require separate IPs for telemetry/metrics ingestion vs model workload egress? Some customers want separate allowlists for high-volume token streams.
2) For ephemeral origin IPs inside Starlight, do you need us to provide a stable NAT gateway in addition to the proxy frontends?

I'll loop netops into the ticket and attach the initial published ranges once available.

—Alice
Netops Lead, Starlight Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@starlighthealth.io>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite proxy + egress IP authorization for private endpoints

Thanks Alice — great answers. A few operational notes from the Dedicated/Private deployment side to make the allowlist as minimal and maintainable as possible: 

- Split control vs data plane: please provide distinct ranges for the control-plane callbacks (auth, attestation, usage-telemetry) vs data-plane egress (generation tokens, model context). We will publish two allowlist entries in Starlight's firewall: "Redwood CP" and "Redwood DP".
- Telemetry separation: we prefer telemetry/metrics over a distinct hostname and IPs so customers can choose to keep metrics on a separate ingress path. If that adds operational burden for you, we can accept a single telemetry host behind the control-plane IPs.
- Minimal set recommendation: if you can supply 3 stable public IPs (2 proxy frontends + 1 NAT gateway) and 2 control-plane callback IPs, that will cover our most common topologies and keep customers from needing per-deployment firewall churn.
- Rotation tolerance: plan for 2-week pre-notice for non-emergency rotations. Anything shorter than 72 hours must be treated as an emergency and will require a formal change advisory.

I've attached controlplane-egress-uri-list.csv with the URIs and sample paths we will call for attestation and config fetch. Also attached a quick draft on the egress-ip-rotation-plan.xlsx with our recommended maintenance window and canary sequence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Starlight netops posts candidate IP ranges into the Jira ticket (INF-2143).
2) Red team to receive the mTLS CA bundle (via secured vault) and confirm cert chain exchange.
3) Ops dry-run targeting 2027-04-07: firewall entries applied in staging, simple curl + mTLS handshake test, verify telemetry flows to the metrics hostname.

If that timeline works, I will own scheduling the dry-run and prepping rollback playbooks.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@starlighthealth.io>, netops@starlighthealth.io
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Satellite proxy + egress IP authorization for private endpoints

Alice — quick operational notes from our SRE side before the dry run: 

- Header expectations: we will include the following headers on all egress calls: X-Redwood-Deployment-ID, X-Redwood-Instance, and a short HMAC (x-redwood-sig) when invoking control-plane URIs. Please let us know if any proxy rewriting will strip or alter these headers.
- Health check IPs: SRE needs a dedicated IP or hostname for active health probes to avoid counting as token traffic on rate-limited proxies. If you can't provide that, we will use the control-plane callback IPs with a dedicated path ("/healthz").
- NAT ephemeral mapping: we accept a small ephemeral port churn but cannot rely on ephemeral random IPs for long-lived customer connections (for customer firewalling). If Starlight cannot provide the NAT gateway option, we will require a static egress IP per deployment.
- Rollout cadence: for the dry-run please apply the candidate ranges in staging only and call out rollback steps. I will include a short checklist in the Jira ticket for ops to execute.

All — final operational checklist from my side before we mark INF-2143 Ready for Staging: 

- Netops action items for Starlight: post the candidate IP ranges in the Jira ticket and confirm the 72-hour and 2-week notice SLAs for emergency vs planned rotations. Provide cert fingerprints and a secure location for the CA bundle.
- Redwood action items: obtain mTLS certs, publish the three header keys to our SDKs, and validate the metrics ingestion host. Priya will lead the SRE dry-run; Marissa will coordinate the timeline with customer success.
- Compliance ask: Karthik, please confirm whether Redwood security requires a signed change advisory (RFC) for any rotation <72 hours. We will hold off final allowlisting until that is confirmed.

I'll set up a short working session (30m) on Friday to walk through the dry-run checklist and to confirm people who will be on the call (netops, SRE, solutions). If no objections I will schedule at 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks everyone — feeling good about the path to staging.

—Jonas
